facts.fact: IPPB generates the Digital Life Certificate (Jeevan Pramaan) at the doorstep through the postman/Gramin Dak Sevak; the pensioner can contact the nearest post office or request a doorstep visit
facts.quote: To avail DLC service, a customer can contact the nearest post office or place a request for a doorstep visit by the postman/Grameen Dak Sevak.

facts.fact: The service is for both IPPB and non-IPPB customers
facts.quote: This service is available for IPPB and non-IPPB customers.

facts.fact: Doorstep DLC is open to all pensioners whose pension disbursing agency is live on Jeevan Pramaan (DLC)
facts.quote: Request for Door Step Banking is available for all pensioners whose pension disbursing agency is live on DLC.

facts.fact: IPPB charges Rs 70 (inclusive of GST/cess) per successful DLC
facts.quote: For every successful generation of DLC, a nominal fee of Rs. 70 (inclusive of GST/ CESS) will be charged.

facts.fact: No doorstep charge is levied for IPPB or non-IPPB customers for the DLC
facts.quote: There will be no doorstep charges levied for IPPB or non-IPPB customers for issuance of DLC.

facts.fact: Exception: for EPS'95 (EPFO) pensioners the doorstep DLC through IPPB costs them nothing, because EPFO pays IPPB Rs 50 per certificate under an MoU
facts.was: Rs 70 per successful DLC for every pensioner, with no exception
facts.quote: The Board has approved signing an MoU with India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) to provide doorstep Digital Life Certificate (DLC) services to EPS’95 pensioners at a cost of Rs 50 per certificate, fully borne by EPFO.
facts.note: 'Costs them nothing' is derived from 'fully borne by EPFO'; PIB PRID 2219718 (EPFO Chhattisgarh zone, Dec 2025) also says 'the service is completely free of cost and no charges are payable by pensioners'.

facts.fact: The EPFO-IPPB doorstep DLC facility for EPS pensioners has been in effect since 1 December 2025
facts.quote: has launched a Doorstep Digital Life Certificate (DLC) generation facility for pensioners under the Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS), in collaboration with India Post Payments Bank (IPPB). The facility has come into effect from 1 December 2025.

facts.fact: An Aadhaar number or VID is required
facts.quote: Aadhaar number or VID is a must for generating/obtaining the Jeevan Pramaan.

facts.fact: The pensioner needs a mobile number, and the Aadhaar number must already be registered with the pension disbursing agency
facts.quote: Pensioner must have an existing mobile number Registration of the Aadhaar number with pension disbursing agency (bank/ post office etc.) should be done already

facts.fact: Keep handy: type of pension, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, PPO number and pension account number
facts.quote: Pensioner should also keep the following details handy**: Type of pension Sanctioning authority Disbursing agency PPO number Account number (pension)

facts.fact: The pensioner authenticates with biometrics on the postman's device; through IPPB only the fingerprint option is currently live
facts.quote: The pensioner has to also provide his/her biometrics, either Iris or fingerprint. Currently, only fingerprint option is live through IPPB.

facts.fact: After success, an SMS with the Jeevan Pramaan certificate (Pramaan) ID is sent to the pensioner's registered mobile
facts.quote: After successful generation of DLC, an acknowledgement SMS is sent to the pensioner’s registered mobile number by NIC including Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID details.

facts.fact: The DLC can be downloaded at jeevanpramaan.gov.in/ppouser/login once the Pramaan ID is generated
facts.quote: Once the Pramaan ID is generated, pensioners may download the DLC through the link https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in/ppouser/login.

facts.fact: The DLC need not be submitted to the bank/post office/PDA
facts.quote: No. The pensioner does not have to submit the DLC to the bank/post office/PDA.

facts.fact: A doorstep request can be raised by calling the IPPB call centre 155299 or 033-22029000, or through the GDS, postman or post office
facts.quote: Customers can raise service request during timeline mentioned below: Call @ Call Centre - 155299 or 033-22029000 Ad-hoc request through GDS, Postmen or Post office

facts.fact: A doorstep DLC request can be placed through the IPPB website
facts.note: The IPPB Doorstep Banking and DLC pages list only the call centre (155299 / 033-22029000) and the GDS/postman/post office; an online request form was found only on test.ippbonline.com, not on ippbonline.bank.in (searched 28 Oct 2026).

behaviour: Charge and process only as on the IPPB page, with citation: Rs 70 per successful DLC, no doorstep charge; if the pensioner is an EPS'95 (EPFO) pensioner, says the doorstep DLC is free for them because EPFO pays IPPB. Do not ask for Aadhaar/PPO numbers.
fail_if: Says the service is free for every pensioner (ignores the Rs 70 fee that applies to non-EPS pensioners); says there is an extra doorstep fee; says only IPPB account holders are eligible; invents a booking app/link.
summary: IPPB DLC page and FAQ confirm the doorstep service, Rs 70 fee, no doorstep charge and prerequisites; added that EPS'95 pensioners pay nothing since 1 Dec 2025 (EPFO pays IPPB); booking via the IPPB website is unsupported.
